note: The three berries of the land, and what each foretells (canon: .spw/surfaces/berries.spw). Read by the game (pie-game.mjs: what a berry does in the lanes) and the pages (Boof's map, the almanac). Each berry is a kind of prophecy as much as a fruit: the boonberry foresees kindly, the baneberry foretells chaos that comes because it was said, the boneberry promises nothing and feeds you honestly. Whether a boonberry's voice is a sensation, a memory, or a thing that literally happens is never settled; the prose keeps both open.

boon.name: Boonberries
boon.look: teal and amber, lit from within; a little borrowed summer kept under the snow by the torch-ants
boon.prophecy: kindly: a boonberry shows the way something will go well, a moment before it does
boon.ambiguity: Boof cannot tell whether she remembers it or it happens to her twice; the book never says
boon.in_the_lanes: filling, and a glimpse: a teal way up the lanes, the clear one, before you reach it

bane.name: Baneberries
bane.look: plum-black, a cold violet sheen, a thorn on the stem; what Mr. BaneWAP is made of
bane.prophecy: chaotically: a baneberry says what will go wrong, and it goes wrong because it was said
bane.self_fulfilling: a foretelling acted on is a foretelling kept; BaneWAP's schemes are baneberry prophecies he announces until they come true
bane.unsaid: squashed underfoot, its prophecy goes unsaid; sweetened by a slice, it says something kind instead
bane.in_the_lanes: a berry that gets past the pie foretells a knock in its lane, and the knock comes because it was said; squash it and it never says; sweeten it and it foretells a boonberry

bone.name: Boneberries
bone.look: bone-white with a dusk-red blush, firm, a faint smoke to the skin
bone.prophecy: none: a boneberry promises nothing and feeds you exactly what it shows, a whole meal in a berry
bone.savoury: savoury, filling, nourishing; it tastes of what the region it grows in would otherwise have had to raise and kill, so nobody has to
bone.in_the_lanes: crust and filling both, and fed: steps tilt less and the pie settles sooner for a while
